<div class="hero"><h1>Framework</h1>
<p class="lead">This page covers the route from data to management advice, the standard of good practice, the crosswalk of method attributes, and the structure of each catalogue entry.</p>
<div class="jump"><span class="label">On this page</span><a href="#route">From data to advice</a><a href="#practice">Good practice</a><a href="#crosswalk">Crosswalk</a><a href="#catalogue">Catalogue structure</a></div></div>

<div class="band" id="route"><h2>From data to management advice</h2>
<div class="intro"><p class="lead2" style="margin:0">Stock assessment and management are iterative processes, in which data and assessments evolve continuously. The toolbox builds users' capacity to understand their data, run assessment methods themselves and with greater confidence, and turn results into management advice and action.</p></div>

<div class="band tint" id="practice"><h2>One standard of good practice</h2>
<p class="sub">Risk equivalence holds only if every assessment informing advice passes the same scrutiny. The toolbox adopts four objective properties of a plausible model (Carvalho <i>et al.</i>, 2021), and no single diagnostic is used alone to accept or reject a model. Each property is checked at the workflow step where it matters most.</p>
<div class="pl4"><div class="plaus">Plausibility<small>Consistency with biology and exploitation history: the overarching check</small></div>
<div class="four">
<div class="fo" style="--c:#0f766e"><h4>Fit to the data</h4><p>Do residuals and fits show that data are represented?</p><span class="stp" style="--c:#0f766e">Understand data</span></div>
<div class="fo" style="--c:#2b6fd6"><h4>Convergence</h4><p>Does the model reach a stable solution?</p><span class="stp" style="--c:#2b6fd6">Run assessment methods</span></div>
<div class="fo" style="--c:#2b6fd6"><h4>Model consistency</h4><p>Do results hold when data are removed or retrospectively added?</p><span class="stp" style="--c:#2b6fd6">Run assessment methods</span></div>
<div class="fo" style="--c:#8e44ad"><h4>Prediction skill</h4><p>Can the model predict data it has not seen?</p><span class="stp" style="--c:#8e44ad">Management advice and action</span></div></div></div>
<p class="ref">For surplus production models these properties are made operational in good practice guidelines (Kokkalis <i>et al.</i>, 2024). The <b>model acceptance checklist</b> applies them across the toolbox.</p></div>

::: {.band .tint #crosswalk}
## Crosswalk

The crosswalk lists every tool in the catalogue with its attributes, so assumptions and data requirements are explicit. Users can filter by attribute and open each tool's catalogue entry. It is a screening aid and does not rank methods.

```{r}
#| echo: false
source("R/toolbox.R")
m <- read_methods()
tab <- data.frame(
  Tool = link_name(m, "../"), Class = m$class, `Sub-class` = m$subclass,
  Application = m$application, Bayesian = m$bayesian, `State space` = m$state_space,
  `Multiple indices` = m$multiple_indices, `Multi-gear` = m$multi_gear,
  `Dome selectivity` = m$dome_selectivity, check.names = FALSE)
DT::datatable(tab, rownames = FALSE, escape = FALSE, class = "compact stripe hover",
  options = list(paging = FALSE, scrollY = "380px", scrollX = TRUE,
                 scrollCollapse = TRUE, dom = "ft",
                 language = list(search = "Filter tools:")))
```

::: {.callout-note}
## One source of truth
Generated from [`data/methods.csv`](https://github.com/Henning-Winker/nfifm-toolbox/blob/main/data/methods.csv), which also drives the [method selector](../select/index.qmd) and the attribute row on each method page. Edit one row and all three update on the next build. The [full crosswalk](crosswalk.qmd) lists every attribute.
:::

```{=html}
<div class="tbx p-framework"><div class="band" id="catalogue"><h2>Catalogue structure</h2>
<p class="sub">Every method has a standardised catalogue entry that guides responsible use by documenting data needs, pre-processing, model assumptions, sensitivities, misuse prevention, and available resources. Each entry follows the three key steps of the workflow, from understanding data through running the method to management advice and action, with use and misuse guidance and case studies alongside.</p>
<div class="ovb"><b>Method overview</b><span class="cf">Family / class</span><span class="cf">Method name</span><span class="cf">Short description</span><span class="cf">Main outputs</span><span class="cf">Typical use case</span></div>
<div class="pipe">
<div class="pc" style="--c:#0f766e"><div class="ph">1 · Understand data</div><div class="pb"><p><b>Data.</b> Requirements, method-specific template and preparation.</p><ul class="bl"><li>Minimum data</li><li>Preferred data</li><li>Optional auxiliary data</li><li>Data quality considerations</li><li>Pre-processing steps</li><li>Standardization needs</li><li>Aggregation / binning choices</li><li>Fleet / gear handling</li><li>Missing data handling</li></ul></div></div>
<div class="pc" style="--c:#2b6fd6"><div class="ph">2 · Run assessment methods</div><div class="pb"><p><b>Method.</b> Software or app, settings and assumptions.</p><ul class="bl"><li>Key parameters</li><li>Priors / fixed inputs</li><li>Error structure</li><li>State-space formulation</li><li>Implementation notes</li><li>Core assumptions</li><li>Software / tools</li></ul></div></div>
<div class="pc" style="--c:#8e44ad"><div class="ph">3 · Management advice and action</div><div class="pb"><p><b>Outputs.</b> Diagnostics, sensitivities and the advice outputs support.</p><ul class="bl"><li>Main sensitivities</li><li>Likely violations</li><li>Expected bias</li><li>Warning signs</li><li>Advice suitability</li></ul></div></div></div>
<div class="alg"><div class="al2" style="--c:#b23b3b"><b>Use and misuse</b><p>Guidance alongside every step.</p><span class="cf">Do not use when</span><span class="cf">Common misuses</span><span class="cf">Pre-use checklist</span><span class="cf">Pre-run checks</span></div><div class="al2" style="--c:#4a5d6c"><b>Case studies and references</b><p>Worked examples and primary literature.</p><span class="cf">Applications / case studies</span><span class="cf">References</span></div></div>
<div class="exs"><div style="--c:#1d7a4a"><b>Suitable example</b>Worked example where data are broadly consistent with the core assumptions.</div><div style="--c:#b7791f"><b>Assumption sensitivity</b>Short demonstrations of key sensitivities, diagnostics and likely failure points.</div><div style="--c:#b23b3b"><b>Unsuitable example</b>Data or configurations that violate assumptions and may induce bias.</div></div></div>
</div>
```
